observations: Torah #115 is a short sippur (personal narrative) in which Rebbe Nachman describes his practice of choosing a derech (path) of avodas Hashem and persisting in it firmly for a long period, refusing to be distracted by competing thoughts suggesting he switch to a different approach. Only after considerable time would he reassess and potentially adopt a new path. The text contains zero bechina statements and no conceptual identity mappings. The key themes — hischazekus (strengthening), derech yesharah (upright path), machshavos (distracting thoughts), and emunah in one's chosen approach — are presented as practical advice, not as parallel-aspect relationships. Therefore, no bechina-based packages can be formed, and no new packages are proposed.
